service: Intensive behavioral therapy (IBT) for obesity, face-to-face counseling visit
vignette: 64-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes treated with metformin. Three weeks ago at her family medicine practice her BMI was measured as 30.0 kg/m2 (weight 86.7 kg, height 1.70 m), and she began intensive behavioral therapy for obesity with a dietary assessment. Today is her third weekly face-to-face visit in the first month, with the practice's nurse practitioner, who assesses her eating and activity, gives personalized advice, agrees on goals, teaches self-monitoring techniques, and schedules the next visit. She is alert and fully competent.
rationale_note: Boundary: BMI exactly 30.0. Third weekly visit in month 1, by an NP in a family medicine practice. Type 2 diabetes on metformin is a distractor.

service: Intensive behavioral therapy (IBT) for obesity, face-to-face counseling visit
vignette: 70-year-old man with hypertension and prediabetes, seen by his general internist at his primary care practice. His BMI is calculated at 29.6 kg/m2 (weight 90.6 kg, height 1.75 m). The internist begins intensive behavioral therapy, completing a dietary assessment and a counseling session following the 5-A framework, and plans weekly visits for the first month. He is alert and fully competent.
rationale_note: BMI 29.6 is below the obesity threshold of 30, despite comorbid hypertension and prediabetes.

service: Intensive behavioral therapy (IBT) for obesity, face-to-face counseling visit
vignette: 67-year-old woman with a starting BMI of 34 kg/m2 who began intensive behavioral therapy for obesity 7 months ago with her general internist at her primary care practice. She attended weekly visits in month 1 and every-other-week visits in months 2-6. At the six-month visit the internist reassessed her obesity and documented in the office record a weight of 88.0 kg compared with 91.0 kg at the start, a loss of 3.0 kg. Today, in month 8, she attends a monthly face-to-face counseling visit with the internist. She is alert and fully competent.
rationale_note: Boundary: month-8 monthly visit with exactly 3.0 kg weight loss over the first six months, documented at the six-month reassessment.

service: Intensive behavioral therapy (IBT) for obesity, face-to-face counseling visit
vignette: 72-year-old man with a starting BMI of 36 kg/m2 who began intensive behavioral therapy for obesity 8 months ago with his family physician at his primary care practice. He attended all weekly visits in month 1 and every-other-week visits in months 2-6. At the six-month visit the physician reassessed his obesity and documented a weight of 104.5 kg compared with 107.0 kg at the start, a loss of 2.5 kg. Today, in month 9, he attends a monthly face-to-face counseling visit. He is alert and fully competent and reports improved energy.
rationale_note: Only 2.5 kg lost over the first six months, so the month 7-12 monthly visits are not covered.

service: Intensive behavioral therapy (IBT) for obesity, face-to-face counseling visit
vignette: 66-year-old woman with a starting BMI of 33 kg/m2 who began intensive behavioral therapy for obesity 6 months and 2 weeks ago with a physician assistant at her family medicine practice. She attended weekly visits in month 1 and every-other-week visits in months 2-6. The six-month visit note documents a counseling discussion but records no weight, no BMI and no determination of weight change since the start of therapy. She says she 'feels lighter.' Today, in month 7, she attends a monthly face-to-face counseling visit. She is alert and fully competent.
rationale_note: Month-7 visit, but the six-month office record contains no weight or weight-loss determination; nothing shows she failed to lose 3 kg.

service: Intensive behavioral therapy (IBT) for obesity, face-to-face counseling visit
vignette: 78-year-old woman with a BMI of 38 kg/m2, currently in a skilled nursing facility for rehabilitation after a hip fracture. Her attending physician, a geriatrician, visits her at the skilled nursing facility, performs a dietary assessment, and begins weekly face-to-face intensive behavioral counseling sessions for obesity there using the 5-A framework. She is alert and fully competent. The request is for the first weekly visit.
rationale_note: Counseling delivered in a skilled nursing facility, which the NCD lists as not a primary care setting.

service: Intensive behavioral therapy (IBT) for obesity, face-to-face counseling visit
vignette: 81-year-old woman with a BMI of 35 kg/m2 and moderate-to-severe Alzheimer's dementia, seen at her family medicine practice by her family physician. During today's visit she is disoriented to time and place and cannot follow the conversation. The physician measures her BMI, completes a dietary assessment with her daughter, and provides intensive behavioral counseling on diet and exercise to the daughter. The request is for the first weekly intensive behavioral therapy visit.
rationale_note: Patient is not competent and alert at the time of counseling; counseling is directed at the daughter.

service: Intensive behavioral therapy (IBT) for obesity, face-to-face counseling visit
vignette: 69-year-old man with a starting BMI of 37 kg/m2 who began intensive behavioral therapy for obesity 10 weeks ago with his family physician at his primary care practice; he is now in month 3. He attended weekly visits in month 1 and has been seen every other week since. His most recent face-to-face counseling visit was 7 days ago. He returns today for another face-to-face counseling visit because he wants extra support with meal planning. He is alert and fully competent.
rationale_note: Month 3 allows one visit every other week; this visit is only 7 days after the previous one.

service: Intensive behavioral therapy (IBT) for obesity, face-to-face counseling visit
vignette: 61-year-old woman (Medicare through disability) with a starting BMI of 41 kg/m2 who began intensive behavioral therapy for obesity 3 months and 2 weeks ago with a physician assistant at her family medicine practice. She attended weekly visits in month 1 and every-other-week visits since; her last face-to-face visit was 14 days ago. She also takes a GLP-1 receptor agonist prescribed by her physician and has a consultation with a bariatric surgeon scheduled next month. Today the physician assistant reviews her food log, adjusts her exercise plan, and schedules the next visit in two weeks. She is alert and fully competent.
rationale_note: Month-4 every-other-week visit 14 days after the last, by a PA in a family practice. Concurrent GLP-1 medication and a pending bariatric surgery consult are distractors; the NCD does not restrict them.

service: Intensive behavioral therapy (IBT) for obesity, face-to-face counseling visit
vignette: 73-year-old man seen by his general internist at his primary care practice to begin intensive behavioral therapy for obesity. The note records his weight as 102 kg; his height is not recorded, and no BMI appears in the note or anywhere in his chart. The internist completes a dietary assessment and a counseling session using the 5-A framework and schedules weekly follow-up for the first month. He is alert and fully competent.
rationale_note: Weight is recorded but height and BMI are not, so obesity (BMI >= 30) cannot be confirmed; nothing contradicts it.
